land.text: England as conquered by William between 1066 and the fall of Ely in early 1071

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of England row has shapes 1066-1071 and then none until 1210.

land.text: continental Normandy, which Cliopatria folds into its Norman England row from 1072

predecessors.note: The duchy did not end: William was duke of Normandy and king of England.

land.text: England and the Welsh March, which Henry II took with the crown on 25 October 1154; Northumberland and Cumbria were still Scottish until 1157

successors.note: Cliopatria ends its Norman England row in 1168 and puts England in its Angevin Empire row from 1169; Normandy had been Geoffrey of Anjou's since 1144.

capitals.name: Westminster (London)
capitals.note: The page gives the coronation at Westminster Abbey on 25 December 1066 ('acclaimed King of England and crowned by Ealdred') and does not use the word capital; the Norman court was itinerant and William spent more than 75 per cent of his time in France after 1072. Rouen, where Henry I's body was taken in 1135, is the Norman seat in France.

rulers.name: William I (the Conqueror)
rulers.note: Crowned 25 December 1066; reign from 1066, clipped here to the state's start; 'William succeeded to the throne of England on his father's death in 1087' (William II page).

rulers.name: Henry I
rulers.note: Crowned 5 August 1100; died 1 December 1135; Duke of Normandy 1106-1135 (infobox).

rulers.name: Stephen of Blois
rulers.note: Crowned 26 December 1135; died 25 October 1154. The Anarchy, 1135-1153, contested the throne with Matilda.

keyframe_review.note: 172,201 km2 for 1072-1084: England, the Welsh March cells, and continental Normandy (148 cells in France), because Cliopatria's Duchy of Normandy row ends in 1071 and 'after 1072, William spent more than 75 per cent of his time in France', as 'largely absentee' ruler of both. The page gives no area, so there is no infobox comparison; England alone is about 130,000 km2 and Normandy about 30,000, which fits. The Welsh March (earldoms of Chester, Shrewsbury, Hereford) is named on the Norman invasion of Wales page without dates.

correction.text: the 1085 shape as drawn, for 1085-1086 only; from 1087 see norman-england_1087

keyframe_review.note: 182,668 km2 for 1085-1093, adding 35 Welsh cells (Powys, Pembrokeshire and neighbours). The shape is right for 1085-1086 only: 'William succeeded to the throne of England on his father's death in 1087, but Robert inherited Normandy', so from 1087 the French cells belong to Robert Curthose (new keyframe norman-england_1087). The Welsh cells are unverified: 'unverified: page budget'; no page opened dates a Norman conquest of Powys or Pembroke (the Norman invasion of Wales page is silent on Brycheiniog and gives only 1081 and 1108).

correction.text: England and the Welsh March of the 1085 shape without Normandy, which Robert Curthose held 1087-1105 (with William II as pledgee 1096-1100)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1087-1093: England and the Welsh cells without Normandy. 'William succeeded to the throne of England on his father's death in 1087, but Robert inherited Normandy'; in 1091 William invaded Normandy, 'crushing Robert's forces and forcing him to cede a portion of his lands', but the page does not say which, so no land is moved. Cumberland and Westmorland are added by the 1092 ledger gain, not here.

minus.text: the Welsh cells (north and mid Wales) that Cliopatria adds in 1094 and removes in 1099

correction.text: England, the Welsh March and Cumbria of the 1094 shape, without Normandy (Robert's) and without the north and mid Wales cells, which are an occupation

keyframe_review.note: 199,097 km2 for 1094-1098, the largest Norman England shape: adds Cumbria (19 cells, matching William's building of Carlisle Castle in 1092 and his control of Cumberland and Westmorland) and 37 north and mid Wales cells. The page has William 'less successful in extending his control into Wales' ('two forays into Wales in 1097', 'Nothing decisive was achieved'), and the Norman invasion of Wales page dates neither the 1094 revolt nor the recovery ('by 1101' the Welsh 'had regained control of the greater part of their country'); Cliopatria leaves Gwynedd and Powys with no shape for 1094-1098. The Welsh cells are therefore drawn as an occupation (hatched), not as Norman land, and Normandy is Robert's.

correction.text: the 1099 shape without Normandy, which the ledger gives back to Henry I in 1106 and takes away again in 1144

keyframe_review.note: 186,788 km2 for 1099-1146. Without Normandy at the start: Robert held it (William II had it in pledge from 1096 until Robert returned in September 1100), and Henry I took it at Tinchebray in 1106 (infobox 'Duke of Normandy 1106-1135'); Henry's reunification, the loss of Northumberland and Cumbria to the Scots in 1139 and of Normandy to Geoffrey of Anjou in January 1144 are ledger events inside this shape. The 42 Welsh cells of the 1094 shape are gone (the Welsh recovered Gwynedd and Powys). No infobox area on the pages.

correction.text: England and the Welsh March of the 1147 shape without Northumberland and Cumbria, held by the Scots until 1157

keyframe_review.note: 148,892 km2 for 1147-1151: England and the Welsh March only, so Normandy is gone three years after Geoffrey's January 1144 Rouen. But Northumbria and Cumbria were Scottish: the Treaty of Durham effectively granted them to David and his son Henry (the page: 'would effectively be granted to David and his son Henry'), until 1157. Without them.

correction.text: the 1152 shape without Northumberland and Cumbria, for 1152 to 25 October 1154 only

keyframe_review.note: 148,892 km2 for 1152-1168, the same cells as 1147. The shape is right for 1152-1153 only (without Northumberland and Cumbria, Scottish until 1157): Stephen died on 25 October 1154 and Henry II 'became King of England', so England is Angevin from then (keyframe angevin-empire_1154 in the angevin-empire dossier, which draws Cliopatria's Norman England 1152 shape from 1154); this dossier ends in October 1154. Cliopatria keeps Norman England to 1168 and adds England to its Angevin row only in 1169.

region.text: England, the Welsh March and Normandy under William I

ledger.note: 1072: the Norman conquest is complete and England and Normandy are one Norman dominion. William 'was not secure on the English throne until after 1072'; the last English resistance, on the Isle of Ely, ended in early 1071; 'after 1072, William spent more than 75 per cent of his time in France'. Cliopatria starts its Norman England row in 1072 with England and Normandy together; William was crowned on 25 December 1066 (the Kingdom of England row runs to 1071).

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's 1072 shape

ledger.note: 1072: Normandy passes into the Norman England row. The Duchy of Normandy row ends in 1071; William, duke of Normandy and king of England, was a 'largely absentee' king after 1072, spending three quarters of his time in France. The page does not describe the union directly.

region.text: the Welsh cells (Powys, Pembrokeshire and neighbouring cells) that Cliopatria adds in 1085

ledger.note: 1085: Cliopatria adds 35 cells in mid and south-west Wales to Norman England. The page is silent on Brycheiniog and on Pembroke before 1108 ('moves by Henry from 1108 to settle Flemish emigrants in England into southern Pembrokeshire'); it names the Marcher earldoms and gives William I's 1081 armed pilgrimage to St Davids. The year is the shape's; the Brycheiniog dossier dates the Norman conquest of Brycheiniog to 1088-1093.

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: 1087: William the Conqueror dies; his sons divide the Anglo-Norman dominion. 'William succeeded to the throne of England on his father's death in 1087, but Robert inherited Normandy.' Normandy is Robert Curthose's until Henry I takes it at Tinchebray in 1106.

region.text: Cumberland and Westmorland, the Cumbria cells Cliopatria adds in 1094

ledger.note: 1092: William Rufus builds Carlisle Castle and takes Cumberland and Westmorland from the Scots. William built Carlisle Castle and took control of Cumberland and Westmorland, which 'had previously been claimed by the Scots' (paraphrase). Cliopatria's Norman England shape grows by these 19 cells in 1094.

region.text: the Welsh cells (north and mid Wales) that Cliopatria adds in 1094 and removes in 1099

ledger.note: 1094: the Normans hold the north and mid Wales cells that Cliopatria adds to Norman England (and takes from Gwynedd and Powys, which have no shape for 1094-1098). The page does not support a conquest: William 'made two forays into Wales in 1097. Nothing decisive was achieved' and he was 'less successful in extending his control into Wales'; the Norman invasion of Wales page leaves the 1094 revolt and the recovery undated. Drawn hatched; the Gwynedd dossier records a Norman occupation of Gwynedd 1094-1099.

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: 1096: Robert Curthose pledges Normandy to William Rufus. Robert 'pledged his lands in Normandy to William in return for a payment of 10,000 marks'; William raised the money by a heavy tax and ruled Normandy as regent. Drawn hatched.

region.text: northern Maine, the Maine cells inside Cliopatria's Norman England shape, secured by William's 1097-1099 campaign

ledger.note: 1097: William Rufus campaigns in the Vexin and Maine. 'William campaigned in France from 1097 to 1099 and secured northern Maine'; he 'failed to seize the French-controlled part of the Vexin'. The page does not say what ground was held.

region.text: northern Maine, the Maine cells inside Cliopatria's Norman England shape, secured by William's 1097-1099 campaign

ledger.note: 1099: the Maine campaign ends: in 1099 he responded to Elias de la Fleche's attempt to take Le Mans (paraphrase). The page gives no treaty.

region.text: the Welsh cells (north and mid Wales) that Cliopatria adds in 1094 and removes in 1099

ledger.note: 1099: the Welsh recover north and mid Wales. The page says the Welsh 'by 1101, had regained control of the greater part of their country'; Cliopatria gives Gwynedd and Powys shapes again from 1099.

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: September 1100: Robert Curthose returns to Normandy and the pledge ends. William Rufus was killed on 2 August 1100; Robert returned in September 1100 (paraphrase). Normandy is Robert's again until 1106.

region.text: Normandy

ledger.note: 1105: Henry I invades Normandy. 'Henry used this as an excuse to invade, promising to restore peace and order'; he invaded again in July 1106. Robert had invaded England in 1101 (Treaty of Alton, in which Henry 'renounced his claims on western Normandy, except for Domfront').

region.text: Normandy

ledger.note: 1106: Henry I defeats Robert Curthose at Tinchebray and holds Normandy. The battle was 'probably on 28 September'; 'Henry kept Robert imprisoned for the rest of his life'.

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: 1106: Henry I reunites Normandy with England. The infobox lists him as Duke of Normandy from 1106 to 1 December 1135; the page says he 'had no way of legally removing the Duchy from his brother' and 'avoided using the title duke' at first.

1135: Stephen of Blois seizes the throne on Henry I's death, the Blois dynasty replacing the House of Normandy within the same realm. 'On Henry's death in 1135, his nephew Stephen of Blois seized the throne'; his coronation 'was held a week later at Westminster Abbey on 26 December'. Matilda's claim begins the Anarchy.

region.text: Carlisle and Cumbria, which David I kept under the first agreement

ledger.note: 1136: David I of Scotland 'invaded the north on the news of Henry's death, taking Carlisle, Newcastle, and other key strongholds', and 'an agreement was made under which David would return most of the territory he had taken, with the exception of Carlisle' (The Anarchy page; Henry I died in December 1135; the page does not date the agreement, the first Treaty of Durham of early 1136). Split by the reviewer of batch eu-11-i from the 1139 event, which had both Cumbria and Northumbria.

region.text: Northumbria, granted to David I's son Henry

ledger.note: 1139: the Treaty of Durham grants Northumbria to David I of Scotland's son Henry. 'Northumbria and Cumbria would effectively be granted to David and his son Henry'; Cumbria (Carlisle) was already David's under the first agreement of 1136 (separate event). The year is that of the treaty's link title; the page gives it nowhere in the sentence.

region.text: the duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle

ledger.note: 1141: Geoffrey of Anjou takes the Norman duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle. Geoffrey 'invaded Normandy again' in 1141 and, during Waleran's absence, took the duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle (page wording closely followed; he had attacked Normandy in 1136 and 1138). Eure stands for the zone.

region.text: Normandy east of the Risle, where Geoffrey was fighting

ledger.note: January 1144: Geoffrey of Anjou enters Rouen and the contest for Normandy ends. 'In January 1144 he advanced into Rouen, the capital of the duchy.'

region.text: continental Normandy and the Maine border cells of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: January 1144: Geoffrey of Anjou takes Rouen and Normandy is lost to the Angevins. Geoffrey was 'recognised as duke of Normandy after taking Rouen in 1144'; Louis VII 'recognised him as duke of Normandy shortly after'. Cliopatria keeps Normandy in Norman England until 1146.

region.text: England and the Welsh March, without Northumberland and Cumbria

ledger.note: 25 October 1154: Stephen dies and Henry of Anjou becomes King Henry II of England; England passes to the Angevin Empire. 'Henry became King Henry II of England upon Stephen's death on 25 October 1154.' The Treaty of Winchester of November 1153 (the infobox calls it Wallingford) had settled the succession.

region.text: England and the Welsh March in 1152-1154

ledger.note: 25 October 1154: the Norman kingdom of England ends with Stephen's death. Cliopatria extends the Norman England row to 1168; the Angevin Empire row has England from 1169.

wars.name: William I's invasion of Scotland
wars.outcome: William marched north against Malcolm III with a land army and fleet in 1072; at Abernethy Malcolm expelled Edgar Atheling and 'became William's man', a 'degree of subordination' of unclear extent (Cumbria and Lothian, or the whole kingdom).
wars.note: No border moved; the Scots are not drawn as a vassal because the page leaves the extent open.

wars.name: Rebellion of 1088
wars.outcome: Odo of Bayeux led the 'Rebellion of 1088' in support of Robert Curthose against William Rufus; William defeated it after Robert failed to appear in England.

wars.name: William II's invasion of Normandy
wars.outcome: In 1091 William invaded Normandy, 'crushing Robert's forces and forcing him to cede a portion of his lands'; the brothers reconciled and William agreed to help Robert recover lands lost to France, 'notably Maine'.
wars.note: The page does not say which lands were ceded; no border is moved.

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish war of 1091-1097
wars.outcome: William repulsed Malcolm III in 1091 ('forcing Malcolm to pay homage'), built Carlisle Castle in 1092 and took Cumberland and Westmorland; Malcolm and his son Edward were killed at Alnwick on 13 November 1093; Edgar conquered Lothian in 1094 and in 1097 'recognised William's authority over Lothian'.

wars.name: William II's Maine campaign

zones.text: northern Maine, the Maine cells inside Cliopatria's Norman England shape, secured by William's 1097-1099 campaign

wars.outcome: William 'secured northern Maine' in 1097-1099 and 'failed to seize the French-controlled part of the Vexin'; in 1099 he answered Elias de la Fleche's attempt on Le Mans.

wars.name: Henry I's conquest of Normandy
wars.outcome: Henry invaded in 1105 and again in July 1106 and defeated Robert Curthose at Tinchebray, 'probably on 28 September' 1106; Robert was imprisoned for life and Henry became Duke of Normandy (infobox 1106-1135).
wars.note: Robert's 1101 invasion of England ended in the Treaty of Alton; the page gives no year for the treaty.

wars.name: Franco-Norman war of 1116-1120
wars.outcome: A wider conflict broke out 'probably in 1116'; Brémule was fought in the summer of 1119; 'In June 1120, Henry and Louis formally made peace on terms advantageous to the English king'.

wars.name: Welsh revolt of 1136-1137
wars.outcome: After Henry I's death 'south Wales rose in rebellion, starting in east Glamorgan and rapidly spreading across the rest of south Wales during 1137'; by the end of 1137 Stephen 'appears to have abandoned attempts to put down the rebellion'.
wars.note: Cliopatria's shapes keep the Welsh cells to 1168; no page opened says how much land was lost, so no border moves.

wars.name: Geoffrey of Anjou's conquest of Normandy
wars.outcome: Geoffrey attacked Normandy in early 1136 and in 1138, took the duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle in 1141 and entered Rouen in January 1144.

wars.name: The Anarchy
wars.outcome: Stephen and Matilda's civil war: David I held Carlisle, Newcastle and by the Treaty of Durham Northumbria and Cumbria (returned 1157); Geoffrey took Normandy (1144); the settlement of November 1153 (Winchester or Wallingford) left Stephen the crown; he died on 25 October 1154.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey fixes the borders of the Anglo-Norman realm on the pages opened: the Scottish border (Cumbria, Northumbria), the Welsh March and the frontier with the French royal domain are approximate throughout.

sources.title: Norman Conquest
sources.note: Founding 1066-1072, Abernethy, absentee rule after 1072; thin on 1085-1099.

sources.title: William II of England
sources.note: 1087 division, 1091-1099 wars, Carlisle 1092, the 1096 pledge of Normandy.

sources.title: The Anarchy
sources.note: 1135-1154: Geoffrey in Normandy, the Scots in the north, Stephen's death.

sources.title: Norman invasion of Wales
sources.note: Thin: the Welsh March and the recovery 'by 1101'; silent on Brycheiniog, Gwynedd and 1094-1098.

notes: Pages: 5 of 5 budgeted (Norman Conquest, William II, Henry I, The Anarchy, Norman invasion of Wales) plus the Angevin Empire page opened for the angevin-empire dossier. (1) End: Cliopatria's row is 1072-1168; this dossier ends on 25 October 1154 (Stephen's death, Henry II king; Angevin Empire page), because England joins the Angevin Empire then and Cliopatria draws it in the Angevin row only from 1169. Keyframes _1147 and _1152 are corrected accordingly, and the angevin-empire dossier carries England from 1154 (keyframe angevin-empire_1154). (2) Normandy: Cliopatria draws one Norman England shape with Normandy for 1072-1146, but the pages have Robert Curthose as duke 1087-1106 (William II holding it in pledge 1096-1100) and Geoffrey of Anjou from January 1144; the ledger removes and restores it. The Duchy of Normandy dossier (eu-10) stops in 1071, so Normandy 1087-1106 under Robert has no state to receive it: a dossier for the Duchy of Normandy 1087-1106 (counterpart 'duchy-of-normandy', Robert Curthose) is needed from eu-10. (3) Wales: the Cliopatria shape adds 35 Welsh cells in 1085 (Powys, Pembrokeshire), 37 north and mid Wales cells in 1094 and removes 42 in 1099, while Gwynedd and Powys have no shape for 1094-1098; the pages opened date none of this (confidence-1 events, 'unverified: page budget'); the Gwynedd and Brycheiniog dossiers have the Norman occupation and conquest from their own pages. The William II page says nothing decisive was achieved in Wales. (4) The Scots: Northumbria and Cumbria go to David I and his son Henry (Treaty of Durham, year 1139 only in the link title) until 1157; Carlisle was taken on Henry I's death (page undated); Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba shapes do not include them, so the Alba dossier must carry the gain. Malcolm III's 1072 and 1091 submissions are not drawn as a vassalage because the page leaves its extent open. (5) No infobox area exists on any page opened, so the factor-of-two check is empty; the shapes are consistent with England (~130,000 km2) plus Normandy (~30,000 km2). (6) 1087-1105 Maine: William's 1097-1099 campaign 'secured northern Maine'; Cliopatria's shape holds the Maine border cells (Sarthe, Mayenne) throughout. (7) Failed or not opened: none failed for this dossier; the Norman invasion of Wales page is thin. Counterparts needing dossiers: duchy-of-normandy continuation 1087-1106 (eu-10); kingdom-of-alba must carry the Northumbria and Cumbria gain 1139 and loss 1157.
